summary: A granite-pier lighthouse in about five feet of water off Fairfield, Connecticut, first lit in 1874; its 1916 keeper drowning gave it a ghost story.

access.note: Offshore, reachable only by boat; dwelling and tower closed. Active aid to navigation; federal property offered at GSA auction (2025 outcome not confirmed).

events.note: Congress makes $55,000 available (after 3 March 1871); foundation work begins 1871
Granite pier finished and dwelling erected 1873
Fourth-order lens fitted with clockwork made at Tompkinsville (per NRHP)
Daboll trumpet with Rider hot-air engines replaces fog bell
Oil engines replace hot-air engines; riprap added
Head keeper Frederick A. Jordan drowned, 22 December 1916
Automated 1971 (NRHP: December; LighthouseFriends: 4 September, crew stayed three more months)
Listed 27 September 1990 (Operating Lighthouses in Connecticut MPS)
GSA online auction; high bid $370,000 per LighthouseFriends; outcome not confirmed

notes_for_editor: Moderate evidence: NRHP, three Light-House Board reports, three Bulletin items, two LoC newspapers, USLHS roster, LighthouseFriends/Lighthouse Digest as secondary. (1) LighthouseFriends says 'privately owned' while GSA (2025) describes a federal auction; the 2025 sale outcome and current owner are unverified. The record's agency/ownership (USCG, federal) may be stale. (2) Jordan's body: Lighthouse Digest says soon recovered, LighthouseFriends says March 1917; Norwich Bulletin 26 Dec 1916 says search had failed. (3) Titles: 1930 newspaper calls W. A. Shackley 'the Keeper' while the register lists him first assistant (head George Petzolt 1929-41); Digest calls Hardwick keeper from 1932 vs register second assistant 1933-41. (4) 1891-92 report OCR reads '9^ miles'; story says 'more than nine miles'; the appendix author is not named in the passage. LHB scan pages given, printed pages not confirmed. (5) NRHP calls the lens both a bullseye lens with clockwork (description) and a fourth-order lens (significance); LF/USLHS say original fourth-order Fresnel. Lens status today not found. (6) Roster names matched by position in USLHS list: Poss (to 1915.03.15), Oliver (1912-), Gage; Dotcher/Dutcher both listed 1910-11. (7) Pauline Jones / Jane Martin: Digest says married to keepers and calls her 'June'. (8) Newspaper snippets read via newspapers.py windows only, not full articles. Newspapers for 1919-1922 (hits found) not read.
